objectClass.notes: Original Eastbrook visual language only. The interaction response is gameplay-authored and no readable text is baked into geometry.

reasoning: Long-distance readability depends on twin floor-seated posts, a broad board, a deep cobalt rain hood, and open ground clearance.
Repeated shingles, parchment cards, pins, corner plates, and masonry courses require deterministic bounded systems.
Rear and grazing views expose roof brackets, rear rails, board depth, and footing contacts for a complete three-dimensional reconstruction.
Stable interaction and notice-surface sockets allow later wiring without coupling gameplay to mesh order.

specDepthDecision.rationale: A flat facade card would fail the roof depth, rear bracing, post separation, stone seating, and future interaction contract.

definitionOfDone: Match the complete 2.4 by 0.6 by 2.6 yard silhouette and player-relative scale across all admitted views.
Preserve twin posts, two stone footings, a deep cobalt hood, front and rear timber frames, blank parchment cards, and restrained gold fittings on Low and Ultra.
Ship at or below 1,200 target triangles and never above 2,500 triangles, with two materials, two primitives, zero embedded textures, zero skins, and zero animations.
Expose stable ground, interaction, and notice-surface sockets plus compound collider metadata for later wiring.

Do not advance a critical feature below 0.7.

proceduralStrategy: Construct every piece deterministically from beveled boxes, shallow extrusions, and bounded repeated clusters.
Lock floor seating, target bounds, player scale, open lower gap, board, posts, and roof depth before detail.
Keep roof-course steps, rear rails, brace overlaps, footing joints, and paper depth ordering as geometry because they affect silhouette or grazing response.
Use a fixed original blank-card arrangement and abstract Eastbrook crest with no readable text or copied decorative composition.
Carry surface identity with semantic vertex colors and one shared external atlas, then merge to one surface and one hardware primitive.
Preserve named interaction and notice-surface sockets plus compound collider metadata independently of mesh order.

referencePbrExtraction.acceptedLimitation: Generated studio pixels contain baked light. Shipping intentionally uses vertex colors, semantic roughness scalars, and the repository shared atlas instead of pretending exact PBR extraction.

mustAvoid: albedo reused as roughness or AO
material differences that vanish on Low
judging material only under one studio setup

referenceCamera.note: Match framing by bounds and view label. Do not pixel-fit baked studio shadows or the scale-guide crop edge.

lightingFromPhoto: Neutral review: broad warm-white key from front-left at elevation 35 degrees, intensity 2.2, with soft shadows.
Fill review: cool hemisphere or broad right fill at intensity 0.8 so hood, rail, and card-board contact cavities remain readable without flattening.
Rim review: restrained cool rear-right rim or environment reflection at intensity 0.6 for posts, roof, and rear-frame separation.
Use ACES-like tone mapping at exposure 1.0, neutral gray background, and soft ground contact shadows beneath both feet; also pass dusk and Low without post effects.

actionReadiness.contract: Expose stable semantic pivots, interaction and content sockets, compound collider intent, and runtime metadata even though the shipping noticeboard is static.
authoringRules: The asset root owns whole-object transforms.
Runtime interaction targets Socket_Interact, not an anonymous mesh.
Future posted content targets Socket_NoticeSurface and Socket_NoticeCards.
Static collision uses the compound proxy and never the visual mesh.
Every child overlap remains gap-free after optimization.

destructionPolicy.debrisStrategy: No shipping destruction; keep seams only as future metadata.

animationAnchors: Socket_NoticeSurface supports future content layers without rebuilding the frame
the shipping asset contains no animation clip or per-frame transform
destructionAnchors: posts, board, roof, braces, and footings retain separate semantic fracture groups in metadata
shipping asset is not breakable and exposes no detachable fragments

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: Merge into one surface and one hardware material bucket, generate repetition through instances before export merge, keep only silhouette and grazing-critical relief, and never remove interaction readability on Low.

same silhouette, board, crest, parchment value blocks, and interaction landmark; shared-atlas micro detail may filter naturally
